target_customer: African merchants, freelancers and consumers sending and receiving cross-border payments
problem: Merchants in Africa could not use PayPal, Venmo or Square, and receiving crypto required complicated exchanges. Flux offered a phone number based wallet for crypto or fiat payments.
business_model: Payments app with transaction fees, later banking and card services

founders.name: Ben Eluan
previous_startups: Joppa (university project that became the basis for Blueloop)

founders.name: Osezele Orukpe
founders.background_notes: YC page lists Blueloop Inc as employer.

founders.name: Israel Akintunde
founders.background_notes: Named as founder by YC page and Disrupt Africa.

competitors.name: Bundle Africa
competitors.what: Crypto and social payments app in Nigeria

technical_complexity.rationale: Wallet creation tied to phone numbers, crypto to fiat conversion and local payout rails require integrations but standard engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Crypto wallets and remittance apps were widely copied and depended on banking partners.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: The Central Bank of Nigeria crypto restrictions in 2021 and a 2024 crackdown hurt the model more than any competitor.

market_need_then: Founders cite no PayPal, Venmo or Square in Africa and a local currency that fell faster than Bitcoin.

identity.visual_style: Blue and white with sun and eye graphics on the site
identity.voice_and_tone: Plain and secure: send, spend, bank and invest from one app

brand_strength.rationale: Generic name shared with many Flux companies; coverage is limited to African tech outlets.

pivots.why: Nigerian central bank crypto restrictions, with a further crackdown in 2024-02 per Techpoint

outcome_analysis: Flux is still operating with about 15 staff as of June 2024. After the YC batch it had about 5,000 users and over $750,000 in volume, but Nigerian crypto restrictions forced a move to fiat banking. Funding beyond the 2020 pre-seed is not public, so its trajectory is stalled or slow rather than failed.
notes: Aggregators list totals of $460K and $125K, unverified; the $125K is YC's standard deal. Technext article returned 403. The $77K pre-seed is also stated in a Techpoint snippet. Techpoint 2024 names LemFi as a much better funded rival, not recorded as it is not dated near the batch. Name origin not found in any source.
